title: Flat finitely presented geometrically integral algebra is projective
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a finitely presented flat homomorphism of commutative rings whose fibre rings $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are geometrically integral over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. Then $S$ is a projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Finite presentation, residue fields, spectra and geometric integrality (of $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the fibre ring over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$) are [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-local-noetherian-approximation], which is the Noetherian approximation paragraph of Tag 05FT. It supplies a cocartesian diagram with R₀ of finite type over ℤ, a finite type flat map R₀→S₀, geometrically integral fibres at every prime of R₀, and S≅S₀⊗_{R₀}R. The approximation lemma applies because the given map is finitely presented and flat and all its fibres are geometrically integral.

source.place: Tag 05FT, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective-nonnoetherian, proof: cocartesian diagram and Noetherian approximation paragraph

proof.text: The ring ℤ is Noetherian (every ideal of ℤ is principal). Since R₀ is of finite type over ℤ, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] gives that R₀ is Noetherian. The finite type flat map R₀→S₀ has geometrically integral fibre rings at every prime of R₀ by Step 1, so [lem-trf-local-noetherian-fibres-projective] gives that S₀ is projective as an R₀-module.

source.place: Tag 05FT, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective-nonnoetherian, proof: apply lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective to S₀

proof.text: The cocartesian square gives an isomorphism of R-modules S≅S₀⊗_{R₀}R, and the symmetry of the tensor product gives S₀⊗_{R₀}R≅R⊗_{R₀}S₀. By [lem-trf-local-projective-tensor-base-change], applied to R₀→R and the projective R₀-module S₀ of Step 2, R⊗_{R₀}S₀ is a projective R-module. A module isomorphic to a projective module is projective (a direct summand of a free module is carried to one by the isomorphism), so S is projective over R.

theorem projective_of_geometricallyIntegral_fibres
    (R : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R B] (hflat : RingHom.Flat (algebraMap R B))
    (hfibres : ∀ (p : Spec (.of R)) (K : Type (max u v w)) [Field K] [Algebra R K]
      (ι : (Spec (.of R)).residueField p →+* K),
      algebraMap R K =
        ι.comp (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)).inv ≫ (Spec (.of R)).Γevaluation p).hom) →
      IsDomain (B ⊗[R] K)) :
    Module.Projective R B
